sources.note: Lists only PARADISEC MR1-097 (Ross 1980 recording 'Eklep Apalik'), Glottolog, Ethnologue and LINGUIST List entries; no language description of any kind.

sources.citation: Spencer, Juliann, Sara Van Cott & Bonnie MacKenzie. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Bebeli. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2013-003. Dallas: SIL International. 96 pp.
sources.note: Appendix D.6 (p. 84 ff.) gives an Aiklep wordlist (Asailo village, 2010, transcriber Wayne Baker) written phonemically (sec. 2.3), with no stress marks; the report contains no statement about stress.

sources.citation: Spencer, Juliann, Bonnie MacKenzie & Sara Van Cott. 2011. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Ambul. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2011-050. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Appendix C.6 (p. 84 ff.): the same phonemic Aiklep wordlist (Wayne Baker, Asailo 2010), no stress marks; text establishes the Ambul-Aiklep-Gimi chain (64% lexicostatistic similarity), cites Hoopert & Wakefield 1980, and mentions existing 'Aiklep literature' (sec. 4.2.9); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1996. Relations among languages of West New Britain: an assessment of recent theories and evidence. In M. Ross (ed.), Studies in languages of New Britain and New Ireland 1, 7-62. Pacific Linguistics C-135.
sources.note: p. 8: 'Until much more detailed accounts of certain languages, such as those now classed as Bibling and Arawe, are published, attempts at subgrouping must necessarily be tentative' — confirms no description of any Arawe language existed; her own Arawe data are basic-vocabulary lists plus Hoopert & Wakefield 1980; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. xiii+487 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Ch. 5 SW New Britain network (printed pp. 160-165, 181-183): Aiklep placed in the Western Arawe chain, a few reflexes cited (e.g. Aiklep wong D:2S), wordlist data in appendix (index pp. 397, 419). No stress statement for Aiklep or any Arawe language; the only 'stress' passages concern Ali (Verner's-law lenition) and Proto Hote-Buang vowel loss.

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Britain. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study vol. 2, 365-386. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.note: p. 370: Arawe divided into eastern (Pililo) and western (Moewehafen); Chinnery's 'Moewe-Haven' wordlist noted; nothing on stress (only a speculative remark about possible phonemic tone in some Whiteman languages, not Arawe).

sources.citation: Chowning, Ann. 1969. The Austronesian languages of New Britain. In Capell, Chowning & Wurm, Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 2, 17-46. Pacific Linguistics A-21. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 3.52-3.53 (printed pp. 29-30): Arawe family = Arawe proper (Pililo) and Moewehafen (the eastern language, = Aiklep/Apalik, with Gimi as a branch); cognate percentages; no phonology and nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page aikl1237 and sil.org / ANU Open Research / ScholarSpace / Wikipedia searches for 'Aiklep', 'Moewehafen', 'Arawe', 'Solong', 'Arove', 'Akolet', 'Wayne Baker'.
sources.note: Glottolog lists 0 descriptive references (only Ross 1988, Chinnery 1928, Chowning 1969, the Bebeli survey, Ethnologue); sil.org has no Aiklep-titled item; ANU has only 'Malcolm Ross tapes'; ScholarSpace nothing; Wikipedia redirects to a West Arawe stub with no phonology.
